verdict.tagline: Vast space exploration hindered by repetitive worlds and endless loading screens.
for_you_if: you enjoy spending hours designing and building custom ships
you find deep outpost customization rewarding
you can look past repetitive procedural exploration
not_for_you_if: you are frustrated by frequent loading screens between areas
you encounter technical instability and crashes on launch
you expect densely populated and unique planets to explore

distortion_flags.sentence: Player positivity increases steadily as playtime grows, despite shared complaints about technical friction and empty worlds.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players face immediate crashes, stiff animations, and constant loading transitions right from the start.

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent crashes when attempting to start a new game from the main menu.

citations.review_text: Crashes every time on my RX 9070 XT when creating a new game. Nice job Todd!
Can't even try. The game crashes when I click "new game".

I avoid buying games when they are brand new to give the developers a chance to patch out any bugs.
This game has been out for three years now and I have finally purchased it.
This game is completely unplayable.
The main menu looks lovely, but pressing new game will cause the game to crash.
I have spent multiple hours trawling through forums trying to find a fix and there just isnt one.
This game maybe be great, but I will never know.

claims.claim: The game features frequent loading screens and cutscenes between areas.

citations.review_text:
This game is a piece of shit. It looks dated, the gameplay is dated and there are loading screens every five minutes. Right after the first space tutorial i knew everything people were saying about this was true. Space travel is just moving around nothingness with JPEG of planets around.

Instant refund. Bethesda is done.

I played this game on Game Pass when it was released, couldn't continue the game after 3-4 hours, it was buggy, performance was bad, and it was a Glorified Loading Screen and Cutscene simulator.

Forward three years later, I bought this game on Steam, found it cheap. Played for 40 or so minutes to come to the conclusion that apart from performance, nothing has changed? Nothing ...

It's still a Glorified Loading Screen and Cutscene simulator with three separate games Stitched together, and still it's buggy, along with lore breaking and immersion breaking gameplay ever, you are the only one with a Space Buggy in all of the 1000s of generated planets where you can only play in a small rectangular area ... What incentive do I have of using the Buggy? Where would I go? You can just skip using it, it's not large enough to use the Buggy to travel, and to find what? A few landmarks? Not worth the trouble ...

It's better if you just play No Man's Sky, that game is a GAME and it's a 1000 times better!

I CANNOT and will NOT recommend this game to anyone ...
ship building is heavily limited, you cant land/take off or fly in atmosphere, and the "flying" is not actually real. You cannot fly to a planet/moon, its all fast traveling/loading screens

claims.claim: Reviewers describe character animations, interactions, and general movement mechanics as stiff, clunky, and outdated.

citations.review_text:
I've only put about two hours into Starfield, so maybe it gets better, but my first impression hasn't been great. The gameplay is painfully boring, and the constant crashes only make it worse.

I've never really minded Bethesda's usual game design in Fallout or The Elder Scrolls, but it's 2026, and the same clunky mechanics, stiff character interactions, and glitchy NPCs are starting to get old. What I could overlook years ago just feels outdated now. I expected more from Bethesda at this point. *Sigh* If only they just focused on ES6 or Fallout SMH

Initially, I was skeptical about all the mixed reviews around Starfield, so I decided to give it a try myself.

I played for about an hour and... why does everything feel so clunky? Character movement, switching weapons, the controls in general. I still can’t believe I have to press Tab every time I want to change a weapon. It honestly feels like some of these controls came straight from the 2000s.

And that’s what makes it even more disappointing, because the game clearly has so much potential. The graphics, textures, atmosphere and overall world look really, really good.

But the controls? Come on, Bethesda. For a game this ambitious, they shouldn’t feel this outdated.

Really disappointed so far.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that if you use a controller, it continuously switches back to keyboard inputs unless you hold down a button.

citation.review_text:
While the graphics are wonderful, the spaceflight mechanics are unintuitive and really rather miserable. They are also rather slow in nature, and if you're using a controller, even if you're not touching a keyboard, it will continuously switch back to keyboard even while the controller is still plugged in, unless you are holding down some button on the controller basically continuously.

The game seems unfinished.

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent loading screens between locations and doors throughout gameplay.

citations.review_text: The game is aesthetically well-executed, but it simply isn't fun. It lacks humanity, human creativity, storytelling, and anything genuinely engaging that would make players want to keep coming back. The loading screens, lack of a proper narrative, and almost nonexistent world-building certainly don't help either.

This is a definite "DO NOT BUY" if i  have to sit thru one more  Go in the door, black screen loading...Go out the door, black screen loading, I'll croak.  i could possibly get thru the numerous loading screens if there was some kind of game play here.  guess what there isnt.  you follow the blue dot, "you talk to someone by answering a question with 1 of 4 responses."  you walk around and guess what.  "you talk to someone by answering a question with 1 of 4 responses."  you jump in your ship and "fly" ( thats a joke, you dont) you hit a button and magically  show up at a planet.  then guess what? you "land" (thats a joke, you dont) you hit a button and you are on the surface.  then guess what..... you follow the blue dot, "you talk to someone by answering a question with 1 of 4 responses."   i kept thinking there was going to be something, because inthe first hour you got to shoot down a few ships (arcadey by fun) you shoot a few pirates.  but nope, Blue Dot, hit a response.  this is nothing more than a graphic novel where you choose what page to turn to.  Sorry Bethesda but you missed the boat and what you claim in your descriptions is false advertising and just out right "deceptive"

TLDR: I tried; but I can't make the game fun.

Pros: 
- Occasionally looks pretty

Cons:
- Overwhelming and unfulfilling inventory management
- Load screens
- Boring story
- Horrible introduction

Avoid this game

Starfield: 1000 Planets, 3 Things to Do

Regret: 106% (4.81 euro per hour, the most expensive loading screen in my library)

Starfield promised 1000 planets to explore. It delivered 1000 planets with the same abandoned lab on each of them. Most of my 11 hours were spent watching loading screens between doors. There are good moments, and the ship building is actually fun. But at 4.81 euro per hour, it's the most expensive loading screen simulator I own. Todd Howard lied to me again.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that planets feel empty with repetitive procedural generation and reused locations.

citations.review_text:
I do like the game. The first time I gave it a chance, I feel like I already had the mindset that this was a bad game from what I heard about it. After coming back to it again, I enjoyed it a lot more. There's still some slow parts, and parts that could've been done better, but there's also good to it. My biggest gripe is the outpost system, which just feels vastly inferior to the settlement system in Fallout 4. 

There being so many planets, all of which are procedurally generated does feel boring at times, but honestly, I feel that way about Fallout sometimes. Each has extremely boring areas, some interesting, and the important main areas. It just sticks out more in Starfield because there's so many more empty areas. It seems like a "make your own fun" idea that doesn't land well because of the limitations of the outpost system. 

So far I haven't completed the story. I focused on the Free Star missions and I'm now starting the Tracker missions. I had fun with the Free Star missions, so I hope the rest will be the same.

I tried to like this game but i can't even skyrim and fallout 4 are better than this.

If they didn't spend all of that time making 1000  Procedural generated planets with nothing on them and instead focused on hand crafting 6 planets it could have been good maybe the writing would have still been awful , i have never seen such bad writing in a single piece of media in my life,
i have read hundreds of books and played so many games and i have never thought this game would top halo 5 as the worst writing in a video game i have ever played.

The writing in this game summed up"Wow look at this cool thing isn't it cool and im going to tell you why it is so cool instead of showing you"

Problems from fallout 4 were repeated and somehow worse in starfield so I have zero hope for elder scrolls 6.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that performance is poor, with stuttering and lag occurring even on low graphical settings.

citations.review_text: Performance is terrible, the game stutters and lags even on potato settings.  This game needs a serious patch upgrade to make it playable.
All this time later, all these updates, and it still runs poorly. Borderline unplayable.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical instability involving game crashes that prevent normal play.

citations.review_text: I have vivid memories of the first area of this game. This is because I replayed it multiple times as it crashed over and over again. I did manage to get out eventually after a few patches, but the damage was done. Any anticipation or excitement was dead, and I only managed to get a little bit further then acquiring the first ship before I quit for good. It's a regression in most every way from any former Bethesda game, with vast areas of the planet more empty then the void of space, and the worst part is how they handled this. Instead of apologizing they decided to monetize modding, literally trying to profit off of a broken game from other people's work who would only be paid nickels on the dime, if that. I find the monetized modding the worst offender of this game, and I can only hope it is a fad that dies quickly. If you want to allow modders to monetize their work, fine, but trying to build a live service game out of others work is the laziest business practice I can recall at this time, and one I refuse to interact with. On the plus side, this is the game that broke my habit of pre-ordering. So that's a lesson I needed to learn at some point.
Game crashes after tutorial but tutorial lasts long enough to invalidate you for refund. DONT BUY

i could never figure how to get this game to run. it always crashes after like 10mins. i have tried every work around. i know all bethesda games are buggy but this is literally unplayable. i really wanted to love it but it is literally the worst game i every attempted to play. i have great cpu & gpu i should be able to play this game!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the interface is unhelpful and relies on annoying sound effects for menu navigation.

citations.review_text:
The game is absolutely annoying for UI. Each button creates a little warble high pitched noise. This is not acceptable. This compounds as ANY movement of the mouse/controller to navigate through menu triggers this noise.

TLDR: Avoid this game until the devs actually allow settings for AUDIO to disable specific things. It should not require a community mod to disable menus making irritating noises.

Whoever came up with the lockpick system deserves to be whipped.
UI looks cool but everything else is purely trash.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe frequent loading screens interrupting the gameplay when moving between locations, ships, and planets.

citations.review_text: good space rpg even with all the loading screens

Absuolute crap, THESE loadingscreens are awful. More time is spent on loading than actually flying an airship
LOADING SCREENS!
30hrs wasted 
Just go play No Man Sky

I've changed my review to recommended.

The (really )good:
They should have made it just an open world shooter, because the many cities and tons of locations look really great and offer very decent combat moments. 
Physics, movement and controls are spot on.. The amount and quality of details is breathtaking.
Some places feel as stunning as in cyberpunk 2077.

The fubar:
Everything space travel related is ridiculous, because you can't space travel.
You can't approach, land or explore planets by ship. That's all handled by cut scenes and loading screens.
So all you do is fast travel. And navigating through the space map is a bit clumsy and takes a while to get it.

If you can ignore the screwed space thing and familiarize with fast travel (that can be done from almost every spot, not only from within the ship) you get a very cool shooter with stunning and precise visuals in a sheer endless world. I really started to like this game, contrary to my previous opinion.

Should they, in the foreseeable future, add true exploration by ship and some vehicles, then this
would become an absolute mother of a game.

Runs super beautifully in 4K all settings on Ultra on my 5090 RTX notebook.

at the end of the day its a game on bethesdas trash engine from 2011, so everything u do requires a loading screen, get in your ship *loading screen* get in the cockpit and choose a planet *loading screen* appear in space over the planet, try to land *loading screen* get out of the cockpit, leave your ship *loading screen* walk into the city, walk in a building *loading screen*. It was ok in 2011 when i was in elementary school, it is not ok in 2026. any game no matter how entertaining will be tainted by the abomination they call the creation engine. NUFF SAID

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight ship building as one of the standout, highly enjoyable features of the game.

citations.review_text: I just cannot recommend this game....I tried to enjoy it but, the only thing I enjoyed was the ship building....

Disclaimer: I rebought the game on steam and have hundreds more hours on Xbox.

The story is bad. The characters are bad. Balance is bad. Why didn't they use the junking system from Fallout 4 so that all the items in the game are still useful in some way?
Ok. Bad things are out of the way.

The good is that this is literally the only game of it's type outside of maybe No Man's Sky. No other game has the ship building, ship to ship combat, boarding actions, sandbox survival, and rpfps elements all in one place. It's a massive sandbox for you to do whatever you want all the time. Does putting that many things in one game make it kind of shallow in places? Sure. On the other hand, Starfield gives me a fix of all the things I love in one place that I can't get from games that are legitimately in my top 10 games I've ever played.

(Base Game only, completed main story) While I am posting a positive rating, I cannot recommend paying full price for this game (I purchased during the recent sale). With a significant discount the game was worth it for time and effort, but ultimately disappointing for a Bethesda title.

The Good:
*Beautiful world, seeing it is a visual treat
*Solid game play, very similar (see below) to other Bethesda RPG control schemes
*Detailed Character creation, as well as weapon customization
*Ship customization is brilliant, one of the best aspects of the game

The Bad:
*Writing is weak, weaker than any other Bethesda game I've played. It feels like they had a great idea, and just decided to leave it as a simple tale when it could have unfolded into so much more.
*Skills: Very annoying skill progression, particularly when so many game functions are trapped behind two sets of crafting (researching each upgrade type then crafting. Rinse and repeat for 3 tiers).
*Game economy: Earning credits feels like an extra grind between bounties and missions, with very few paying out well. You can make money from selling loot but the vendors run out of money quickly. Ships are so expensive that I used the starting ship and just built/upgraded as I went because it was significantly more cost effective. I did not purchase a single pre-fabricated ship in the game, which was a shame because some looked impressive.
*Story and replay: They make the story seem so significant early game, then as you progress it just becomes mundane, and then rather abruptly concludes with some grand philosophical concept. You can continue with a NG+ but after starting one I have found there is nothing worth the grind.
*Game mechanics: While the gameplay is sound, it's almost an EXACT copy paste of the control scheme and physics of Elder Scrolls and Fallout. For as much as they touted and advertised that this was going to be a genre defining game, all we got was Elder Scrolls V.V: Space Oblivion.

O…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that planet exploration can feel repetitive because many worlds are procedurally generated and largely empty.

citations.review_text:
They clearly went with quantity over quality and you can feel it after a few first hours.

The amount of planets is incredibly large but very rarely do they contain anything important on them.

Additionaly each of them is procedurally generated and it is impossible to explore them fully because of the sheer scale.

Pairing that with Bethesdas' obsession with repeatable quests it makes it uncear which ones are important and which ones are pointless fillers.

I expected a cool space exploration game, instead I got a game where 90% of planets are empty dead rocks, 9% is filled with never ending quests that feel pointless and only 1% is actually worth doing.

It's annoying and made me stop asking vendors for jobs, because I can't be sure if it will be worth my time.

I'm probably in a minority in this but if somebody is like me this is your warning.

Also don't get me wrong I'm stil going to play it because I paid for it. I'm just saying that anything beyond faction and main quests is a 50/50 to be just trash repeatable.

Starfield – Disappointing and Boring

Starfield is one of the most disappointing games I've played. The world feels empty, exploration gets repetitive very quickly, and most planets have very little worth discovering. The loading screens are everywhere, the combat gets boring, and the dialogue often feels lifeless. For a game that promised so much freedom and exploration, it feels surprisingly soulless. After a while, everything starts to feel like the same missions repeated over and over again. Starfield had so much potential, but it fails to deliver a truly exciting space adventure. Definitely not worth the hype there ones was

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface relies heavily on nested menus and prioritizes stylization over functionality.

citations.review_text:
Man this game is such a weird bummer.  I don't wanna feel like I'm just jumping on the hate bandwagon, but I really tried to give it a fair shake.  First of all, it's been 4 years since release, so they've had *plenty* of time to fix all of what I'm about to say.

The user interface itself is a masterclass in bad design.  All the game's menus are annoying and badly designed, and it doesn't feel like an accident...  stylization was overwhelmingly prioritized over functionality, down to the *main* menu with "inventory" and "missions" and such being a circle...  with labels that DON'T SHOW UP other than the currently selected option.  It took me a bit at first to even figure out that *was* a menu.  There are weird quirks like a short delay when closing the menu, that RESETS if you hit gamepad-B again, so if you spam it, you can indefinitely block the menu from actually exiting...  and you *will* be spamming B, since there are so many nested menus in menus you have to deal with.  It's incomprehensible how this UX could have come from humans who tie their own shoes in the morning.

The gunplay is probably this game's strongest aspect, and it's just bad, but like, regular amounts of bad, I guess.  Why put thin-railed handrails all throughout the game, for example, if no care is given to them having proper hitboxes?  There's also this horrific volumetric dust/fog in every indoor area, which makes it obnoxiously hard to see anything you're shooting at at any distance, and just makes the game ugly as heck.

The story and plot beats I've encountered have all been disappointing, and the dialogue writing ranges from ok to rancid.  Some situations are just complete nonsense, like the bartender who tells you that a patron of his had racked up a large bar tab before disappearing, so he wants *you* to pay the guy's tab in exchange for a lead on where to find him.  How would that even make sense?!?  Every bit of "lore" feels so haphazardly slapped together.  And then the dialogue bu…

It is not a horrible game, there is things to enjoy for sure. It is a gorgeous game on my machine and have not experienced big crashes or tech issues.  Still have it's fair share of bugs, but most are in the hillarious department of a companion talking to you and then suddenly mid sentance, getting launched of the face of the plant for no reason.  But there are just too many small annoyances. The UI is Horrid. The companions and most quest are uninspired. When i add it all up together even with getting it on sale I would find it hard to reccomend.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that resources weigh a ton and you cannot easily store them, leading to inventory hell.

citation.review_text:
Inventory hell - you have resources that you cannot easily store and they weigh a ton on the bottom line. Your ship has limited space as well. Why would someone create such a system is beyond me - did they think it would be fun?
Most quests are generic - put that thing over there, get this for me. You run a logistics company that for some reason is well paid
The game is playable but lacks the soul of previous Bethesda games. There is a lot that could and should be fixed, I see no  point in that inventory system. If someone wanted it to be realistic, get to assign someone to do legwork and you just mark resources while they carry them around and become available in a couple of days...but otherwise, no reason to have such a system. We play games to have fun, not to do repeated tasks in order to gain virtual benefits

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the world and exploration feel empty, with repetitive and copy-pasted facilities, locations, and procedural points of interest across planets.

citations.review_text:
Sorry for bad english.

Had hoped it would be Skyrim in space. With lots of fun quests.
Where choices had consequences. Example having to decide between the rivaling factions.
But the world is emty and repeating. And from my experience all quests exist in a vacuum. 

Lots of loading screens for everything. Limited and annoying outpost and house furnishing, very limited and frustrating outpost building. You can`t even build a space station.

Flying your spaceship is just a loading screen. exept when having a scace fight. 

And where are all the settlements. Few cities and does that exists are very small. 
Example the Capital to the Freestar Collectiv Akila City is a small village with a landing zone. And Neom is basically an oil rig with a boring night club and a shopping street. And United colonies have 1 town and its the capital the other town is just a mine with a shop and bar. 

Many of the NPC`s force you to be a good guy or they hate you. very limited what you can do and decide. 

Overall the game just makes me frustrated.

I want to like this game, but it has a lot of weirdly avoidable gameplay blunders, and is generally unplayable without mods.  For the blunders, well, it's extremely repetitive.  You will see the exact same buildings all over the place, and once you go inside, they're identical down to the placement of a random lime or fallen pencil.  There are also a lot of different menus you can go into, and many of them use different keys to move through them for no reason!  For left right, you have Q-T, A-D, and Z-C, probably more, I'm not going back to check at this point.  For mods, I suggest no carry limit, speed up airlocks, speed up cruise mode, speed up mining, skip all the unwanted animations you want (they're not loading screens, just impediments!), and easy digipick for locks.  You'll also want to grab the third  ground vehicle, and then, because all the ground vehicles are undrivable for more than ten feet, the mod that lets you boost as long as you want (you can boost forward, and also up, so together you can fly over all the annoying rocks and trees).  Also, you're going to want to queue up a page of console commands, if only because there are so many times your character would get stuck somehow, or because a quest glitched.  Oh, plus all the people are animated strangely.  And the ship builder is hard to use.  Good luck!

This game could have been the next mass effect instead we get a mostly empty universe with the same science lab over and over again. Then they try to sell us more content for an already empty game. Bethesda use to be one of my favourite game companies now they are the absolute worse.

Starfield is incredibly boring and repetitive. Exploring different planets quickly becomes a tedious cycle of visiting copy-pasted facilities, killing the same space pirates, collecting loot, and repeating the exact same experience elsewhere. For a game set in such a vast universe, there's a surprising lack of creativity and variety. Hostile alien creatures are scarce, planets feel lifeless, and most side quests are uninspired and uninteresting. The photo-taking mechanic is also completely pointless. Why include a feature that lets you take pictures of locations when you can already do that with countless other apps? It's an unnecessary gimmick that adds absolutely nothing meaningful to the gameplay. The game confuses quantity with quality. Having hundreds of planets means very little when there's barely anything interesting to discover.

[h1] A CANVAS THAT OFFERED SPACE FOR YOUR CONTRIBUTION, BUT ISN'T APPEALING ENOUGH FOR PEOPLE TO CONTRIBUTE IN [/h1]

I've thought about writing a long essay about all of the things this game did right and wrong, putting it in bullet points and all that, but I then figured that these sums up this game pretty well:

The core idea seems to be quite straightforward: this game is your typical Bethesda experience that was meant to be shared with the community, for the people to pour their creativity alongside what the devs made, yet it has nearly zero pull and appeal to make most of them commit to it. I'm not sure if its the creative direction or if the team lacks what the previous ones has, but everything that this game offered, outside of it's technological advancement (graphics, support for new tech, higher fps support, etc) is watered down and worse than what its predecessor has, this game has less story, less agency and less uniqueness, and due to all of that, it also has less community support.

The story is so watered down and short, the writing is safe and sterile, conflict felt fake at times and your choice doesn't matter the majority of the time, a far departure from the previous title's immersiveness and freedom. And then there's the gameplay, it's been improved but the loop is downright attrociously repetitive, majority of the things you encountered during exploration are procedurally generated, but they only made 1-2 templates for all of them, which means, everything you encountered will only have 1/2 variants, once you found an abandoned military base, you've found all of them, same enemies, same layout, same loot table. When this is all they have to offer in the base game, I can see why most people aren't necessarily interested into putting more work on it.

If they wanted to attract more talanted people to create for this game, they needed a really good hook to pull people in, yet, instead of making appealing product that allows its community to contribut…

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight ship building as a standout feature, praising the modular creation and customization options.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Ich wollte eigentlich nur kurz mein Schiff umbauen – plötzlich waren drei Stunden weg.[/h1]
Ganz ehrlich: Allein für den Schiffsbau hat sich Starfield für mich schon gelohnt. Es gibt kaum ein besseres Gefühl, als Modul für Modul sein eigenes Traumschiff zusammenzuschrauben, danach selbst durch die Gänge zu laufen und es im ersten Raumkampf direkt auf die Probe zu stellen.
Natürlich machen auch die Quests und das Erkunden Spaß, aber am Ende ziehe ich doch immer wieder im Editor meine Runden und optimiere noch ein letztes Detail. Wer gerne tüftelt, wird dieses Spiel lieben. Klare Empfehlung! 🚀

I love this game. I was an early adopter of it and have played it off and on since launch. On Steam I have almost 150 hours since repurchasing after moving from Xbox to use the Creation Kit. I have over 600 hours on the Xbox version. 

There are some legitimate gripes:
-loading screens
-performance and optimization, specifically for NVIDIA DLSS users
-procedurally generated world tiles and POI’s 
-Updates and DLC content
-base building

Was the game oversold to the community, yes. 

With that out of the what my first 450 hours was done on the vanilla game, minimal creations and no mods. The game isn’t for everyone but if given the chance it creates a world that is compelling and very rewarding. The ship building system is second to none and transcendent with mods. 
The combat is great, the zero G combat physics are exceptional and immersive. If you are judging the combat on other BSG games it far outperforms any Fallout game in the series. 
With the latest Free Lanes and Terran Armada updates it feels more like the game they promised us.

There are a huge amount of safe and valuable mods out there that create such an amazing experience with a community that loves the game. I’d recommend it to anyone who enjoys exploration, space travel, and forging their own story.

If it's your bag, you can have a great time with it. Ship building is fantastic. Movement and combat is a straight upgrade from its predecessors. Companions are more reactive than they've ever been. It has some of the best quest design and writing that Bethesda has ever put out (Vanguard questline, Help Wanted, Lost and Found, Entangled). Looking around in the environments, its easy to tell from all the detail-work that the team is filled with serious space nerds, which I find endearing. It's also a gorgeous game.

It also has some blatant shortcomings that probably should have been addressed before launch. Proc gen means that sometimes POIs are slapped down on planets they have no business being on. The outpost development system is very silo'd from the rest of the game. The Astral Lounge, and Neon in general, is goofy as hell. There was no codex at launch (there is now). The Freestar Ranger questline implicitly promised a mech fight that was NOT delivered on (IYKYK). 

It's a big enough game that if you look for the bad or the good, you'll find it. It is the same tier of "mid" to "pretty good" as Skyrim and Fallout 4 before it. Meet it where its at, and you can have fun.

[h1]Flawed. Frustrating. Unique.[/h1]

Starfield is a game of opposites. For every great thing about the game, there is an equally frustrating or bad thing about it. I have gone through 2 playthroughs of the game, totalling close to 1000 hours,, and it is only now that I can say that I love the game, despite its flaws.

[h2]The Good[/h2]
The game has a lot to love. The worlds are genuinely beautiful. The graphics, while a bit dated, are great. It has its own aesthetic in terms of style. Gunplay is pretty good. 

It's a Bethesda Open World with all the bells and whistles. The main story is good - not great - but better than some of Bethesda's previous titles. The side quests are great though. This is very typical of Bethesda Games.

The game has a granular, adjustable difficulty, so you can tailor the experience to suit your tastes. More games should do this. I ended up creating a difficulty reminiscent of "survival" in Fallout 4.

Shipbuilding is honestly my absolute favorite part of the game. I love coming up with new ideas and making crazy ship builds come true.

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
From how Starfield came out, you can tell a couple of different things: It's clear that the game changed directions several times during development. This is evident in the systems that went into the game, only to be taken out again, but leaving behind traces. 

Fuel economy is a good example. Originally, fuel was meant to be a resource you had to manage. In order to go deeper into the unknown, you'd have to actually secure sources of fuel. The further you got away from settled space, the more this would be a challenge. This got toned down to basically nothing. Which takes us to the next system that got newtered.

Outposts were supposed to serve several purposes. Extraction of fuel and raw resources, automated processing of said resources, and enabling you to build a network of outposts, allowing you to reach the furthest corners of space. That's all still there... excep…

I played a ton of Starfield at launch and I can understand why a lot of people don't like Starfield. The game is absolutely a bit of a mess BUT it is still fun. I have been playing a bit of No Man's Sky and Elite Dangerous and although those games are fun space games, Starfield did do some things right and its a fun game too.

One thing I really enjoyed about Starfield was the ship building. The ship building was legitimately fun for a while. I liked making crazy huge ships. The ship combat isn't even bad either. It would be more fun if there were more types of enemies to fight though. This game needs aliens.

Another thing that Starfield does well is allow you to be a criminal. Being a pirate is really awesome you can just board, loot and steal any ship but the game only lets you have like 10 ships maximum by default. But you can use a console command to allow more. The command is SetGS uSpaceshipMaximumOwnedSpaceships <number> You have to reenter the command each session though. I set mine to 100. I accumulated like 40 ships from pirating but eventually I started seeing the same ships over and over so I stopped stealing them.

One major thing I wish they did better in Starfield is the Outposts. I don't know if they ever fixed them but for me the supply chains never worked right. I spent dozens of hours building outposts on different planets only to not be able to connect resources. It would just do all kinds of unintended behavior instead. Outposts were completely broken at launch and I'm not sure they ever fixed it. It would really add value to the game if they fixed that stuff because outpost building was fun too.

After playing other space games I may come back to Starfield again one day to finish my playthrough. I got all the way through the story and all faction quests except the corporate questline. I eventually got bored after discovering all of the planets and many of the side quests are uninteresting as well. In fact the faction quests are pretty bad too.…

Flying your spaceship is just a loading screen. exept when having a scace fight. 

And where are all the settlements. Few cities and does that exists are very small. 
Example the Capital to the Freestar Collectiv Akila City is a small village with a landing zone. And Neom is basically an oil rig with a boring night club and a shopping street. And United colonies have 1 town and its the capital the other town is just a mine with a shop and bar. 

Many of the NPC`s force you to be a good guy or they hate you. very limited what you can do and decide. 

Overall the game just makes me frustrated.

Massive, Captivating Universe That Still Needs a Little Polish

UP SIDE
Starfield is an incredibly ambitious RPG that delivers an immersive and vast space-exploration experience. The sheer scale of the universe, the depth of the ship-building mechanics was my favorite.

Engaging in intense space dogfights, or following the sprawling faction questlines, there is an immense amount of high-quality content to enjoy.

DOWN SIDE
However, that massive scope comes with a familiar caveat: the game is still noticeably buggy. While none of the glitches completely broke my experience, you will still frequently encounter technical hiccups, odd visual stuttering, companion AI pathfinding issues, and occasional menu quirks.

Building complex outposts was a total miss, instead of feeling like a rewarding sandbox feature, establishing and managing outposts turned into a tedious, exhausting grind for resources and logistics that sapped the fun right out of colonizing new worlds.

Fantastic game, beautiful beyond measure and filled with places and stories to explore. 
From the sounds of it, it was a very different game on release, the game as it is now when I have played it is top class and best of Beths. 
The worlds are gorgeous from the alien skies to the handcrafted PoI's where everything happens, Mostly it's everything you love from Fallout 4, but with a main quest that compliments the game instead of clashes against it.
Unique and embodied world that gives an experience unlike any other. 

There are some cons, the Outpost system is very bare bones and awkward to use, and the base game UI is very frustrating, but both are answered by mods of which there are many and, it's not like Skyrim didn't have mandatory UI mods either. 

Runs smoother than any beths game on my system too, none of the crash-filled bugginess of Fallout 4,

9/10, Fully Recommend, just be prepared to install 100 mods and occasionally be very frustrated with the building controls and pathing, even after mod UIs.

The game is better than the hate it gets and that was before all the improvements and DLC. Like any game the design comes up short like the point of interests which they have patched in more and reduced the chance of running into the same one soon after seeing it. The glaring issue is the outpost building until the latest DLC had little purpose and still is mostly an XP farm or if you want to do it but the benefits are hardly worth the effort. 

I would give it a 7/10 if scores mean anything on that scale its because outpost building is lacking and outside the main faction story missions and DLC the missions lack the quality you would see in other BGS titles.

They tried to make each playthrough more unique by making it so that enemies dont always drop their gear. So if you want that cool helmet, but dont get it, you have to save scum. Over and over. Loading screen after loading screen, baked into the game loop itself, as you desperately try to loot stuff. 3/4 of my playtime is from staring at the main menu depressed.

I put over 200 hours in when the game first released, but the longer I played, the more annoyed I became. Decided to reinstall and give it another bash ... but it's just as annoying as it was, with apparently no meaningful updates.

Pros:
- The soundtrack is nice
- The 'NASA-punk' aesthetic is excellent
- The shipbuilder is very good (small caveat - no way to track or wishlist ship parts from different sellers)
- I liked the 'perform tasks to unlock ranks' of the skills
- The shooting was decent.
- There's a good selection of weapons, spacesuits, helmets, etc.

Mid:
- The writing is somewhere between dated/uninspiring to good. Main quest is essentially Skyrim, but some of the side quests/faction quests were enjoyable.

Cons:
- Loading screens. Leave your ship ... loading screen. Enter your ship ... loading screen. Enter a small shop ... loading screen.
- You don't land or launch your ship. No in-atmosphere flight. Most space travel is done via the map/loading screen.
- No seamless on-foot exploration. The game loads a terrain 'tile'. Get to the edge of the tile and it will need to loading-screen you into another tile.
- Insipid exploration. I don't mind long hikes (I love No Man's Sky, so I'm happy walking discovering stuff) but buildings & settlements are copy pasted from a 'pool'. Seen one particular layout, it will be *exactly* the same, down to loot *and* clutter.
-No catalogue of flora and fauna I've scanned.
- Inventory management is dated, cumbersome (no pun intended!), and gets in the way of crafting. If you are a resource hoarder like me you and your ship will be encumbered all the time. The only 'vanilla' workaround I found was using a seemingly infinite-storage in the basement of The Lodge, and going there to do all my crafting.
- The crafting is a massive downgrade from Fallout 4. For example, you have to spend resorces to craft iron sights, and the attachment you are replacing just disappears. This is the same for most weapon/suit mods. Having limited-r…

as someone who has like nearly 900 hours in this game on and off. 

I love ship building and space combat type games, this fills that spot slightly I guess, loading screen garbage as usual tho just ruins everything for me.

I absolutely hate Constellation worst faction in all of bethesdas titles (Like I hate constellation more than I hate Railroad from fallout and thats saying alot)

if its on sale for like 10 bucks i'd pick it up, or if you really wanna play the mod Starwars: Genesis which is a 10/10 then buy it.

I've played this game for quite a while; I've played through some of its good pieces and its bad ones. But here is how I would sum it up, categorized into good and bad. 

Good:

The game has some pretty in-depth quests, and some are a ton of fun to play through.
The modding support is huge. With the right mods, it becomes so much more fun.
There's more, but they're not necessarily notable. 

Bad:

The main questline is horrible. It's the same copy-and-paste thing over and over again, and you have almost no motivation to do it except to finish the game. The side quests are somehow better, like way better. Some quests could serve as the main plot if they decided to make it that way. 
Almost everything you do requires walking through doors that greet you with a black loading screen. 
The NPCs are just plain stupid. You literally figure out the reason for a potentially humanity-ending problem, practically end piracy, and kill some of the Settled Systems' most ferocious beasts. A random marine will tell you, "I don't have time for tourists."

I know the bad outweighs the good in this review, but I still enjoy the game and have had a lot of fun with it.

But don't buy it if you don't like doing the same thing over and over.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe encountering game-breaking bugs and quest glitches that block progress and force restarts.

citations.review_text: I came into this game knowing it was a viewed as a disaster. I went in done the initial Vectera intro and when I arrived at at Kreet I realized that this would've made an excellent sandbox exploration game like minecraft/terraria/starbound but it leaned to heavy into strict linear narration. Constellation is the biggest culprit. they punish you for doing faction questlines that doesn't fit their approval. Gamers don't want to be lectured by essential story npcs when they want to have fun. What is a game if it isn't fun...a job. THAT ISN'T WHY WE PLAY GAMES BETHESDA! But honestly I honestly I'm not mad at that. What I am mad at is the fact that there a bug that prevents you from proceeding the crimson fleet storyline...two words...Jade Swan! That stupid ship never appears. I done everything beforehand all quests without mods yet this stupid ship never appears no matter how many new games or new game plus i run crimson fleet is just impossible to finish. No modders can figure it out due to how complex ships are because they are made like buildings so you can't just spawn it in you can't coc tp into it because said building isn't in a single cell it must appear so you can enter. Bethesda this game had potential but modders just aren't invested enough to fix your mistakes on this and i don't blame them. You made it too hard to fix. And EVERYONE knows that "Bethesda never fixes their own games" so i ask you how long do you expect the modding community to fix your mistakes without actual pay without appreciation without YOU doing the work you are paid to do. 0/10 don't waste your money.

This would be a decent port of Fallout if it were fan-made.  As a full price offering from a major game studio, it's terrible.  So many terrible bugs.   I had almost made it through the main campaign when I encountered a game-breaking bug that has apparently existed since launch.  Scripted enemies didn't spawn, even with earlier saves. Never fixed.  It forced me to restart completely if I wanted to actually be able to complete the main quest.  

Ten or so hours into my next playthrough, I encountered yet another game-breaking bug.   A different one.  Suddenly I can't craft or upgrade anything for the rest of the game.  This bug has also existed since launch.  

Three years after launch, but still having the same bugs that completely destroy all progress.

The game is enjoyable to a point. But there are also a ton of glitches. My playthrough has become unplayable due to a quest bug in the main quest. Also the scaling and leveling is either way to difficult or way to easy. I really hope ES6 will live to the reputation Bethesda is supposed to have. Also the story and characters are so incredibly bland. Only the spaceship mechanics are worth a shot.

How is this game soooo damn broken on PC after all this time. I know it didn't review well and had issues at launch, but I played it though with little issue. Now, when I want to revisit to check out the DLC I paid for, the game is broken. I keep running into game breaking issues and I'm sick of it. How can the experience be sooo much worse years after release. Can't progress passed an early game mission to run the Red Mile, its just stuck!! I shouldn't have to reference a dozen online articles to figure out how to get passed your broken crap.

As everyone else has stated, 99% of everything aside from the quest areas are copy and paste buildings. This game should NOT lock you out of achievements for using certain commands. I've had to reload way too many times due to broken quests or getting stuck in between railings. I'm also sick of being locked out of certain dialogues, items, or quests because the game wasn't clear on how exactly you get them. This game isn't a very replayable game, so I just end up moving on without half of the content this game has to offer.
